x: The Punchhi Commission (2007) was the second major commission on Centre-State relations and federalism, after Sarkaria. Election funding was the Indrajit Gupta Committee's subject.
t: Discriminate the Centre-State commissions from the electoral reform committees.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) dealt with State funding of elections, not Centre-State relations. Rajamannar (Tamil Nadu), Sarkaria and Punchhi did deal with federal relations.
t: Find the committee on electoral reform.

x: Both are true: the Inter-State Council rests on Article 263, and it was set up on 28 May 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's advice. The date and recommendation do not explain the constitutional basis, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a date and a recommendation explain a constitutional basis.

x: Punchhi dealt with federal dialogue and coordination, Sarkaria recommended a permanent Inter-State Council, Rajamannar was Tamil Nadu's push for autonomy, and Indrajit Gupta covered election funding. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Match each committee to its subject.

x: A is true: the President set up the Inter-State Council by order under Article 263. B is false because Parliament did not create it by law.
t: Recall that the Inter-State Council was set up by Presidential order.

x: The Article 371 special provisions are in Part XXI, 'Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions'. Part XX is amendment.
t: Discriminate Part XX (amendment) from Part XXI (special provisions).

x: Article 371 allows separate development boards for Vidarbha and Marathwada (Maharashtra) and for Saurashtra and Kutch (Gujarat). Hyderabad-Karnataka comes under Article 371-J.
t: Pair Article 371's regions with Maharashtra and Gujarat.

x: Both are true: Article 371-A protects Nagaland by shielding Naga customs and religious practice, customary justice, and land ownership from Parliament's laws unless the Assembly agrees. R explains A.
t: Recall what Article 371-A protects.

x: Article 371-A covers Nagaland, 371-B Assam, 371-C Manipur, and 371-D Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. The answer is a-b, b-i, c-a, d-c.
t: Recall the order of 371-A to 371-D: Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, AP and Telangana.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Central University in Andhra Pradesh comes under Article 371-E. Article 371-D ensures fair opportunities in jobs and education across regions of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
t: Discriminate Article 371-D (jobs and education) from 371-E (Central University).

x: Article 371-E lets Parliament set up a Central University in Andhra Pradesh. The 30-seat minimum is Goa (371-I), and the tribal committee is Assam (371-B).
t: Recall Article 371-E.

x: Article 371-G protects Mizoram's religious and social practices, customary law and land ownership, as 371-A does for Nagaland.
t: Pair Article 371-A (Nagaland) with 371-G (Mizoram).

x: Both are true: Article 371-H gives the Governor of Arunachal Pradesh special responsibility for law and order. R states what that special responsibility is.
t: Recall Article 371-H.

x: Article 371-I says Goa's Assembly must have at least 30 members, below the usual minimum of 60.
t: Recall the Article 371 exceptions to the 60-seat minimum.

x: Article 371-F covers Sikkim, 371-G Mizoram, 371-H Arunachal Pradesh, and 371-I Goa. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the order of 371-F to 371-I: Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal, Goa.

x: Article 371-J provides for the development of the Hyderabad-Karnataka (Kalyana Karnataka) region. Vidarbha and Saurashtra come under Article 371.
t: Recall Article 371-J.

x: All four pairs are correct: 371-A is Nagaland, 371-B Assam, 371-C Manipur, and 371-H Arunachal Pradesh.
t: Recall each Article 371 State.

x: Both are true: Article 371 covers Maharashtra and Gujarat, and Article 371-A covers Nagaland.
t: Recall each Article 371 State.

x: Article 371-B provides Assam's tribal-area committee, 371-C Manipur's hill-area committee, 371-F Sikkim's incorporation, and 371-J Hyderabad-Karnataka's board and reservations. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Discriminate Assam's tribal-area committee from Manipur's hill-area committee.

x: Article 371-F covers Sikkim's merger into India (36th Amendment, 1975), its Assembly size and governance. Option A describes 371-D and B describes 371-G.
t: Recall Article 371-F.

x: Both are true: the 98th Amendment (2012) inserted Article 371-J, which gives the Hyderabad-Karnataka region reservations in education and jobs. What the Article does does not explain how it was inserted, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether an Article's content explains the amendment that inserted it.

x: Both are true: Article 371-J's Hyderabad-Karnataka region has six backward districts, and the Article provides a development board and reservations for it. The provisions do not explain the number of districts, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a provision's content explains a count.

x: Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes come under Part X, Article 244(1) and the Fifth Schedule. Tribal areas of the North-East come under Article 244(2) and the Sixth Schedule.
t: Discriminate Article 244(1) (Fifth Schedule) from 244(2) (Sixth Schedule).

x: Option C is incorrect: declaring a Scheduled Area does not end the State's executive power there. That power continues, subject to the Fifth Schedule, and the area does not become a UT or a new State.
t: Recall that State power continues in Scheduled Areas.

x: Both are true: every State with Scheduled Areas must have a Tribal Advisory Council (Fifth Schedule, para 4), which advises on tribal welfare. What it does does not explain why it is required, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a body's function explains why it must exist.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Governor, not the Chief Minister, reports on the administration of Scheduled Areas, directly to the President, every year or whenever asked.
t: Recall who reports on Scheduled Areas and to whom.

x: Under paragraph 5 of the Fifth Schedule, the Governor can make regulations to stop or limit tribal land passing to non-tribals and to control money-lending to Scheduled Tribes.
t: Recall the Governor's regulation powers under the Fifth Schedule.

x: In Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997), the Supreme Court held that transferring or leasing tribal land in Scheduled Areas to private companies for mining is void under the Fifth Schedule.
t: Recall the Samatha ruling of 1997.

x: A is true: the Fifth Schedule comes under Article 244(1) in Part X. B is false because the Sixth Schedule comes under Article 244(2) and is also linked to Article 275(1).
t: Discriminate Article 244(1) (Fifth Schedule) from 244(2) (Sixth Schedule).

x: The Fifth Schedule deals with Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes under Article 244(1). The Sixth deals with tribal areas under Articles 244(2) and 275(1). The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Note that each Schedule appears twice in List-I.

x: All four are correct: the Sixth Schedule applies to Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram ('AMTM'), and to no other State.
t: Recall the four Sixth Schedule States.

x: The Fifth Schedule covers 10 States: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha and Rajasthan. Four States come under the Sixth Schedule.
t: Discriminate the 10 Fifth Schedule States from the 4 Sixth Schedule States.

x: Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan are Fifth Schedule States. Meghalaya and Mizoram are Sixth Schedule States. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-i, d-ii.
t: Check each State against the four Sixth Schedule States.

x: Both are true: Sixth Schedule district and regional councils have legislative, executive and judicial powers, and under the Fifth Schedule the Governor oversees land transfers and laws. One Schedule's rules cannot explain the other's, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether one Schedule's rules explain the other's.

x: The Fifth Schedule has the Tribal Advisory Council and the Governor overseeing land transfers. The Sixth has autonomous councils with legislative, executive and judicial powers. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Note that each Schedule appears twice in List-I.

x: I, II and IV are correct: the President declares Scheduled Areas, the Governor reports to the President, and Tribal Advisory Councils advise on tribal welfare. III is false because the Chief Minister does not report to the Home Ministry.
t: Recall who reports on Scheduled Areas and to whom.

x: Manipur is not covered by the Sixth Schedule (it has hill-area committees under Article 371-C), and neither is Nagaland. Only Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram are.
t: Recall the four Sixth Schedule States.

x: Both are true: the Sixth Schedule comes under Article 244(2) and is funded through grants under Article 275(1), unlike the Fifth Schedule under 244(1). R explains A by that contrast.
t: Discriminate Article 244(1) (Fifth Schedule) from 244(2) and 275(1) (Sixth).

x: I and II are correct: Andhra Pradesh is a Fifth Schedule State and Assam a Sixth. III is false because Nagaland is not under the Sixth Schedule, and IV is false because Mizoram is under the Sixth, not the Fifth.
t: Check each State against the four Sixth Schedule States.

x: Telangana and Jharkhand are Fifth Schedule States, and Tripura and Meghalaya Sixth Schedule States. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-i, d-ii.
t: Check each State against the four Sixth Schedule States.
